title: 7 Financial Institutions Hit by AI Hacking... Emergency Meeting Called
key_facts: Seven South Korean financial companies are confirmed to have suffered information leaks.
They are four commercial banks including Shinhan, Kookmin, Hana and Busan, plus Yegaram Savings Bank, Hyundai Capital and, newly, Welcome Savings Bank.
About 2,200 pieces of corporate customer information, such as representatives' names, emails and phone numbers, are estimated to have leaked at Welcome Savings Bank.
The attacks hit the sector at the same time; some institutions blocked their attempts.
Authorities noted that AI tools may have been used; the Financial Services Commission chairman said it cannot be ruled out.
The same attacker IP address appeared at several breach sites; the attackers kept changing IPs and targeted weaker auxiliary systems such as loan-broker web servers and mobile devices.
Banks and card companies must finish emergency inspections by 6 Oct; securities, insurance and savings banks by 8 Oct.
quote_evidence: We cannot rule out the possibility of hacking attacks utilizing AI.
The hackers targeted auxiliary systems with relatively vulnerable security rather than heavily secured payment systems.
Financial authorities have ordered banks and card companies to complete emergency inspections by the 6th, and securities, insurance, and savings banks by the 8th.
why_it_matters_hint: Coordinated breaches across a national financial sector, with AI use suspected but not established.
notes: Follow-up of the 3 Oct pool item on the police probe into AI-driven bank hacks.
